AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It | NVIDIA Blog

For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days.
AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast.
Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time.

Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle.
Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.
Using the NVIDIA cuDSS library, multiphysics software provider COMSOL is accelerating such simulations for semiconductor manufacturing by up to 10x.
By integrating NVIDIA cuDSS, Applied’s Ginestra simulation platform runs up to 10x faster than CPU-only approaches.
And with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, Applied’s ACE+ multiphysics platform delivers topography simulations up to 35x faster.
Siemens is integrating NVIDIA cuLitho into its Calibre lithography software, delivering up to 17x acceleration on key simulation workloads.
As such, faster calculations can help researchers explore material behavior and reaction pathways that influence next-generation semiconductor processes.

Lam Research demonstrated that the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework can predict plasma behavior in milliseconds, compared with days for a full simulation — giving engineers a faster way to explore process conditions without rerunning the full model each time.
